q: For x(t) = u(t) and h(t) = u(t) in a continuous-time LTI system, y(252) is: (spaced-repetition variant 13166)
h: The output is the ramp r(t) = t u(t).
f: Step 1: y(t) = integral from 0 to t of 1 dt = t for t at least 0. Step 2: y(252) = 252. Check: differentiating y returns u(t), the step response relationship h = ds/dt holds.

q: X(s) = 472 / (s (s + 284)). The final value x(infinity) is:
h: Final-value theorem: limit of s X(s) as s tends to 0.
f: Step 1: s X(s) = 472/(s + 284). Step 2: at s = 0 this is 472/284 = 1.662. Check: the remaining pole at -284 is in the left-half plane, so the theorem applies.

q: y[n] - 0.7099 y[n - 1] = x[n]. The pole of H(z) is at z =
h: Transform: Y(z) (1 - a z^-1) = X(z); the pole solves 1 - a z^-1 = 0.
f: Step 1: H(z) = 1 / (1 - 0.7099 z^-1). Step 2: denominator zero when z = 0.7099. Check: this matches the pair a^n u[n] with a = 0.7099.

q: A sawtooth-type Fourier series has harmonic coefficients b_k = 2A/(k pi). For A = 356 and k = 133, b_k is:
h: Substitute A and k into 2A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: b_k = 2 x 356 / (133 pi). Step 2: = 1.704 (4 decimal places). Check: coefficients fall as 1/k, slower than a triangle wave (1/k^2) but faster than the constant spectrum of an impulse train.

q: A DFT uses N = 2048 samples taken at fs = 1421312 Hz. The bin spacing is: (spaced-repetition variant 13166)
h: Spacing = fs / N.
f: Step 1: spacing = 1421312 / 2048. Step 2: = 694 Hz between bins X[k] and X[k+1]. Check: N bins x 694 Hz spans the full 1421312 Hz sampling rate.

q: Output power is 34.49 times the input power. The gain in decibels is: (spaced-repetition variant 13166)
h: dB = 10 log10(P2/P1) for powers (20 log10 is for voltages).
f: Step 1: ratio = 34.49. Step 2: 10 log10(34.49) = 15.38 dB. Check: ratio 0.5 gives about -3 dB and ratio 10 gives +10 dB; sign follows gain versus loss.

q: A 4-ary modulation runs at 3375 baud. Its bit rate is:
h: Bit rate = baud x log2(L).
f: Step 1: bits per symbol = log2(4) = 2. Step 2: bit rate = 3375 x 2 = 6750 bps. Check: denser constellations raise rate at fixed baud but need higher SNR for the same error rate.

q: For A = [[0, 1], [-782, -195]] (companion form), det(A) is:
h: det [[p, q],[r, s]] = p s - q r.
f: Step 1: det = (0)(-195) - (1)(-782). Step 2: = 782. Check: det(A) equals the product of eigenvalues, here the constant term of s^2 + 195 s + 782.

q: For x(t) = 268 cos(2 pi 308 t) (1 ohm reference), the average power P is:
h: P = A^2 / 2 for any sinusoid, independent of frequency.
f: Step 1: identify amplitude A = 268. Step 2: P = A^2/2 = 71824/2 = 35912. Check: average of cos^2 over a period is 1/2, and frequency 308 Hz does not change the average.

q: Evaluate the integral over all t of (t^2 + 532) delta(t - (89)) dt:
h: Sifting: the impulse samples the bracket at t = t0.
f: Step 1: sifting property: integral of x(t) delta(t - t0) dt = x(t0). Step 2: x(89) = 89^2 + 532 = 8453. Check: everything away from t = 89 is multiplied by zero.

q: The system y[n] = x[n] + x[n - 795] is classified as: (spaced-repetition variant 13167)
o: Memoryless and noncausal
Memoryless and causal
With memory and noncausal
With memory, causal, linear and time-invariant
h: It uses the present sample and a past sample only.
f: Step 1: x[n - 795] is a past sample, so the system has memory. Step 2: no future samples appear, so it is causal. Step 3: it is a fixed linear combination with constant coefficients, hence linear and time-invariant.

q: Convolving x[n] = {18, 341} with h[n] = {505, 208} (both starting at n = 0), the value y[1] is:
X(s) = 1 / ((s + 25)(s + 315)) with causal ROC. In x(t), the coefficient multiplying e^(-25 t) is:
h: Cover-up: set s = -a in 1/(s + b).
f: Step 1: partial fractions: A/(s+25) + B/(s+315) with A = 1/(315 - 25) = 0.0034. Step 2: x(t) = (0.0034 e^(-25 t) - 0.0034 e^(-315 t)) u(t). Check: x(0+) = 0, matching the initial-value behaviour of this strictly proper X(s).

q: x[n] = (0.3538)^n u[n]. The sample x[3] is:
h: Cube the base; u[3] = 1.
f: Step 1: x[3] = (0.3538)^3. Step 2: = 0.0443. Check: |a| = 0.3538 is below 1, so the ROC |z| above 0.3538 includes the unit circle: decaying and stable.

q: An odd square wave of amplitude 474 has sine harmonics (4A/(k pi)) sin(k w0 t) for odd k. The amplitude of the k = 3 harmonic is:
h: Substitute k into 4A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: amplitude = 4 x 474 / (3 pi). Step 2: = 201.1718 (4 decimal places). Check: it falls as 1/k, so higher harmonics weaken - the origin of Gibbs ripple concentration near jumps.

q: A 393 Hz tone is sampled at fs = 517 Hz. It aliases to:
h: Fold: alias = |f - k fs| for the integer k giving a result in [0, fs/2].
f: Step 1: Nyquist needs fs at least 786 Hz, so 517 Hz undersamples. Step 2: alias = |393 - 1 x 517| = 124 Hz. Check: 124 lies in [0, 258], the representable baseband.
